title: Credible interval as a posterior region
dek: Wikipedia credible interval: a set with posterior probability 1−α. Not a confidence interval. HPD versus equal-tail is a reporting choice.
story: A credible interval on Wikipedia is a region C(y) such that P(θ ∈ C | y) = 1−α under a named posterior. That is a probability statement about θ after seeing y.
A confidence interval is a statement about a procedure's coverage in repeated sampling. stats-confidence-intervals already owns that. Do not rename one as the other in a TB paper.
HPD (highest posterior density) versus equal-tailed quantiles disagree for skewed posteriors (variance components, rare-variant frequencies).
deep: If the posterior is Beta(a,b), equal-tail uses Beta quantiles; HPD may need numerical work.
Calibration of 80% credible intervals is stats-posterior-calibration.
Transformations: an HPD on logit π is not the HPD on π after pushing through the inverse map.
Empty-looking MCMC 'intervals' from unconverged chains are not credible intervals.

visual.caption: Schematic posterior (tight) versus a prior (wide). A credible interval is a region under the posterior curve, not a sampling-distribution interval for an MLE.
